domain.name: Social Emotional Development
domain.description: Social emotional development is the core of early care and education because it sets a firm foundation on which all other learning will take place.

sub_strand.name: Self-Awareness
sub_strand.description: The child demonstrates an awareness of self. Children develop a sense of personal identity as they begin to recognize the characteristics that make them unique as individuals and to build self-esteem.

indicator.name: Demonstrates self-confidence
indicator.description: Acknowledges her own accomplishments and says, "I can hit the ball." Explains, "I'm learning how to take care of myself and my friends." Signs, "I can do it myself."

indicators.source_text:
Demonstrates self-confidence.
a.
Acknowledges her own accomplishments and says, "I can hit the ball."

indicator.name: Demonstrates developmentally appropriate cultural curiosity and responsiveness
indicator.description: Wonders about a friend's seaweed snack and asks for a taste. The group widens the story time circle to make room for the child and their wheelchair. A guest speaker (parent) shares a storybook and song in their home language to the class.

indicators.source_text: e. Demonstrates developmentally appropriate cultural curiosity and responsiveness.

domain.name: Language and Literacy
domain.description: Environments rich with print, language, storytelling, books, digital tools, and writing materials allow children to experience the joy and power associated with reading and writing, while mastering basic concepts of print.

sub_strand.name: Receptive Language Understanding
sub_strand.description: The child demonstrates understanding of directions, stories, conversations, and nonverbal cues.

indicator.name: Demonstrates understanding of a variety of finger-plays, rhymes, chants and songs, poems, conversations, and stories
indicator.description: Follows gestures and actions. Teacher asks, "Where would you like to play? It's time to work." Child points to blocks or answers, "Blocks." Teacher extends the interaction and builds on child's response by saying, "Oh, you want to play in the block area."

indicators.source_text:
a. Demonstrates understanding of a variety of finger-plays, rhymes, chants and songs, poems, conversations,
andstories.

indicator.name: Holds a book right side up with the front cover facing the reader and understands left to right and top to bottom directionality
indicator.description: Turns the pages one page at a time to continue reading. Turns the book right side up before beginning to look at it, when handed a book upside down.

indicator.description: Finds the front of the book, the first page of the text, and the first word on the page. Points to the first page and says, "Start here."

indicator.description: Makes a book and says, "My book is called My Mom, and I'm the author." Identifies that the illustrator draws the pictures in a book.

indicators.source_text: C. Understands a book has a title, author, and/or illustrator.

indicators.source_text:
a. Differentiates between sounds that are the same and different (e.g., environmental sounds, animal

indicators.source_text: f. Identifies and discriminates syllables in words.

indicator.name: Demonstrates understanding and follows directions that involve one step, two steps, or multiple steps

indicators.source_text: C. Demonstrates understanding and follows directions that involve one step, two steps, or multiple steps.

sub_strand.name: Expressive Language and Communication Skills
sub_strand.description: The child uses verbal and nonverbal communication for a variety of purposes; to share observations, experiences, problem-solve, reason, predict, seek new information, and make connections.

indicator.name: Communicates needs, wants, ideas, and feelings through three to five-word sentences
indicator.description: Engages intentionally in simple or multi-turn conversations with peers and adults at snack time. Talks with a peer about a trip to a park, another child utilizes sign language which includes social rules; pragmatics; age appropriate tone, and volume.

indicators.source_text: a. Communicates needs, wants, ideas, and feelings through three to five-word sentences.

indicator.name: Speaks clearly and understandably to express ideas, feelings, and needs
indicator.description: Combines words into simple sentences - "Is it time to go home?" Or "More milk please." Says, "I want to go play at the water table."

indicators.source_text: b. Speaks clearly and understandably to express ideas, feelings, and needs.

sub_strand.name: Expressive Language and Communication Skills

indicator.name: Makes culturally relevant responses (both verbal and nonverbal) to questions and comments from others
indicator.description: Exclaims, "I did it!" after teacher asks, "Did you get your jacket on?" Says, "I have a cat, too," after teacher shows a picture of a cat. Responds, "¡SÍ, mamá! I have my peanut butter sandwich," during drop off, after a parent asks, ¡Adiós! ¿ Tienes tu sándwich?

indicators.source_text: C. Makes culturally relevant responses (both verbal and nonverbal) to questions and comments from others.

indicator.name: Initiates, sustains, and expands conversations with peers and adults using open-ended responses
indicator.description: Approaches peers and asks, "What are you making?" Says, "I went to the zoo." Teacher expands by asking, "What was your favorite animal?" Child replies, "The lion." Teacher responds, "The lion is your favorite. Why?" Child answers, "I like the way he roars."

indicators.source_text: d. Initiates, sustains, and expands conversations with peers and adults using open-ended responses.

sub_strand.name: Expressive Language and Communication Skills

indicator.name: With modeling and support, child uses language that includes social rules; e.g., pragmatics, appropriate tone, volume, and inflection to express ideas, feelings, and needs
indicator.description: Responds excitedly, "That's my favorite!" when an adult begins to read a book. Tells a classmate emphatically, "Stop, I don't like that!" or whispers in a classmate's ear during circle time.

indicators.source_text:
e. With modeling and support, child uses language that includes social rules; e.g., pragmatics,

indicator.description: Uses turn-taking during conversations with peers and adults. Looks towards her friend, while speaking.

indicators.source_text:
f. Uses culturally relevant responses such as eye contact, turn taking, and intonation while having conversations

indicator.name: Recognizes when the listener does not understand and varies the amount of information to clarify the message
indicator.description: Uses a different word to clarify the intended message when child realizes he has been misunderstood. Points to a picture to clarify his intent.

indicators.source_text: g. Recognizes when the listener does not understand and varies the amount of information¹² to clarify the message.

indicator.name: With modeling and support, uses increasingly complex phrases and sentences
indicator.description: Says, "Let's put the cars up higher on the ramp so they will go really fast."

indicators.source_text: h. With modeling and support, uses increasingly complex phrases and sentences.

sub_strand.name: Vocabulary
sub_strand.description: The child understands and uses increasingly complex vocabulary.

indicator.name: Uses rich vocabulary across many topic areas
indicator.description: Says, "Let me listen to your heart with a stethoscope" while in dramatic play. Reads The Very Hungry Caterpillar and exclaims, "I see a cocoon." The child uses new words or signs during play and other activities.

indicators.source_text: a. Uses rich vocabulary across many topic areas.

sub_strand.name: Vocabulary

indicator.name: Figures out the meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts using the context of conversations, pictures that accompany text, or concrete objects
indicator.description: Explains, "I am making skyscraper," while playing with the wooden blocks. Says, "I will get the colander to rinse the grapes" while playing in the dramatic play area.

indicators.source_text:
b. Figures out the meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts using the context of conversations, pictures
that accompany text, or concrete objects.

indicator.name: Uses category labels and names objects within a category; e.g., fruit, vegetable, animal, transportation
indicator.description: Replies, "I want a carrot," when asked, "Which vegetable do you want?" Gathers a variety of animals and says, "I found a dog, two pigs, and a duck."

indicators.source_text: C. Uses category labels and names objects within a category; e.g., fruit, vegetable, animal, transportation.

indicator.description: Responds to the teacher's requests to return his car to the shelf, put blocks in the container, or stand beside a peer. Says, "I am standing between Billy and Rita."

indicators.source_text:
d. Demonstrates understanding of and uses words that indicate position and direction; e.g., in, on, out,
under, over, off, besides, behind.
